quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the engine should be in:
questions.correctAnswerText: Neutral.
questions.explanation: Always put your motorcycle in neutral before starting the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the dashboard that turns on when the engine is ready to start.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of crashing, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Turn your headlight off during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your headlight off during the day.
questions.explanation: To stay safe, always be visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake lights, and proper lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: When wearing a jacket for protection, the jacket should:

options.text: Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly.
questions.explanation: Your riding jacket and pants should fit snug enough that they don't flap in the wind, but not so tight that you can't move easily.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: Center
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when being passed. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may make the other driver cut back in front of you too soon.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:
questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement is slippery.
questions.explanation: Leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead if the pavement is wet or slippery. You need extra distance to stop safely.

questions.question: __________ can cause motorcycle collisions.
questions.correctAnswerText: Tailgating
questions.explanation: Following too closely behind another vehicle causes collisions. Always keep a safe distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: In any vehicle:

options.text: No one may have an open container of alcohol.
The operator may keep open alcohol if riding alone.
A passenger may have open alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one may have an open container of alcohol.
questions.explanation: No one in any vehicle can drink alcohol or have an open bottle or can. If you're alone and there's an open container in your vehicle, the law says it's yours.

questions.question: To control your motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit with your arms slightly bent. Use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Keep your knees against the tank to stay balanced during turns.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brake at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brake at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time with controlled pressure. Do not lock the brakes.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to grip your hips, waist, or belt firmly. They can also use secure handholds if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: It is illegal to ride a motorcycle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: In California, riders age 21 and older cannot ride with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Riders under 21 cannot ride with a BAC of 0.01 percent or higher. Even below the legal limit, riding after drinking alcohol is unsafe.

questions.question: Traffic lanes moving in the same direction are separated by:
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass. A dashed white line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: Motorcycle mirrors:

options.text: Have blind spots, just like cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots just like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Your lane position when riding a motorcycle:

options.text: Has little effect on whether other drivers can see you.
Is very important because it affects whether other drivers can see you.
Cannot protect you from wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is very important because it affects whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps other drivers see you and helps you see them. Proper positioning also protects you from wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is easiest to see by other drivers when riding in which lane position?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: The center lane position is usually best because it places you in the driver's rearview mirror. Be ready to change positions if traffic or conditions require it.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may proceed through the intersection with caution.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop completely and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: A solid white line on the edge of the road indicates:

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the edge of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Avoid sudden moves because they can cause a skid.
Travel on the shoulder to stay out of traffic.
Use only the rear brake because the front brake does not work on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden moves because they can cause a skid.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, sudden changes in speed, direction, shifting, turning, or braking can cause a skid. Make all movements smooth and controlled.

questions.question: When riding ________, you face the greatest risk of conflict with other vehicles.
questions.correctAnswerText: Near an intersection
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflict between motorcycles and other vehicles. Position yourself where other drivers can see you best when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: As you drink more alcohol, your ability to safely ride:
questions.correctAnswerText: Decreases.
questions.explanation: The skills you need to ride safely get worse as you drink more alcohol. Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.
